samples.summary: Changed bullet-marker color export (`markerToXml` / `buClr`) has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff changes `markerToXml` from `if (marker.color != null) …` to `const buClr = storedColorToThemeColor(marker.color); if (buClr) …`, so bullet colors are now normalized through `toRgbHexColor` and dropped when unnormalizable. I grepped `packages/slides/test/export` for `buClr`, `buSzPts`, `buFont` and `marker:` — no matches; `test/export/pptx/text.test.ts` only exercises `buAutoNum`/`buChar` for list blocks with no `marker` object. The new tests in that file cover run-level `solidFill`/`highlight`/`uFill` only. So neither the positive path (a real `marker.color` like `#FF9900` still emits `<a:buClr><a:srgbClr val="FF9900"/></a:buClr>`) nor the drop path is covered; a regression that silently stops emitting bullet colors would pass CI.

samples.summary: No test that a *valid* alignment value passes the new API validator
samples.evidence: `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` is a new closed set of four values. The new spec tests only (a) a hostile string is rejected and (b) a style with *no* alignment key passes. Nothing asserts that `alignment: 'center'` / `'right'` / `'justify'` / `'left'` are accepted, so dropping a member from the set (e.g. forgetting `'justify'`) would break legitimate PUTs with a green suite.
searchedFor: read docs-content.controller.spec.ts 'docs body shape validation' block (lines 390-525)

samples.summary: DocsFormattingToolbar's reset-to-undefined change is untested; only TextFormatGroup got a regression test
samples.evidence: The diff makes the same `""` → `undefined` fix in two components, but the new `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts` renders only `TextFormatGroup`. I found no frontend test rendering `DocsFormattingToolbar` and asserting `applyStyle({ color: undefined })` / `{ backgroundColor: undefined }` (glob of packages/frontend/tests/**/*docs* shows only docs-context-menu and docs-table-context-menu tests).

samples.summary: Table cell "No fill" UI wiring (now passing `undefined`) has no component test
samples.evidence: The store-level behavior is covered by the new `yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` case, but the menu button that must pass `undefined` instead of `""` is not asserted anywhere: grepping `backgroundColor|No fill|applyTableCellStyle` in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx returned no matches. A revert of the UI line would leave the suite green.

samples.summary: `toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` also passes if the handler passes `{}` (or any object without the key)
samples.evidence: Vitest/Jest's `toHaveBeenCalledWith` uses toEqual-style structural equality, which treats an explicitly-`undefined` property as equal to a missing one. The test therefore cannot distinguish `applyStyle({ color: undefined })` — the shape the store's `removedInlineStyleAttrs` relies on (`key in style && style[key] === undefined`) — from `applyStyle({})`, which would silently NOT clear the attribute. Asserting on `Object.keys(call[0])` / `'color' in call[0]` would make the test actually pin the contract. (It does still catch the `""` regression, so the core case is covered.)

samples.summary: Decorative assertion that holds regardless of the fix
samples.evidence: `expect(docXml).not.toContain('a"/><w:b')` asserts the hostile value does not appear XML-escaped, but neither the old code (bare `.replace('#','')`, no escaping) nor the new code ever escapes it, so this assertion is true in both worlds. The test is still non-vacuous overall thanks to the `<w:shd ` count and the `w:fill="a"/>` check.

`if (channels.some((n) => Number.isNaN(n))) return undefined;` is placed after `Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round(Number(n))))`, and the regex `[-+\d.]+` cannot match a non-numeric channel; no test in color.test.ts or docx-style-map.test.ts exercises it (e.g. `rgb(., ., .)`). Either dead code or an untested edge.

The helper lists seven keys (verticalAlign, padding, borderTop/Bottom/Left/Right) but the new store test only clears `backgroundColor`; a typo in one of the other attribute names would not be caught. Low risk since the mechanism is shared.

finding.summary: Changed bullet-marker color export (`markerToXml` / `buClr`) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff changes `markerToXml` from `if (marker.color != null) …` to `const buClr = storedColorToThemeColor(marker.color); if (buClr) …`, so bullet colors are now normalized through `toRgbHexColor` and dropped when unnormalizable. I grepped `packages/slides/test/export` for `buClr`, `buSzPts`, `buFont` and `marker:` — no matches; `test/export/pptx/text.test.ts` only exercises `buAutoNum`/`buChar` for list blocks with no `marker` object. The new tests in that file cover run-level `solidFill`/`highlight`/`uFill` only. So neither the positive path (a real `marker.color` like `#FF9900` still emits `<a:buClr><a:srgbClr val="FF9900"/></a:buClr>`) nor the drop path is covered; a regression that silently stops emitting bullet colors would pass CI.

verdict.reason: The claim "no test at all" for the changed `markerToXml`/`buClr` export path is false. `packages/slides/test/export/pptx/round-trip.test.ts:154-166` imports the rich fixture's slide 7, exports it with `exportPptx`, re-imports, and asserts full structural equality (`normalize(deckB)).toEqual(normalize(deckA)`). That fixture slide (`build-rich-pptx.ts:417-428`, documented at lines 12-13 and 381-389) deliberately contains `<a:buClr><a:srgbClr val="FF0000"/></a:buClr>` plus `buSzPts`/`buFont`/`buChar`, and the importer maps `buClr` into `block.marker.color` (`src/import/pptx/text.ts:273-274`, `424-428`). The normalizer does NOT strip `block.marker` (`normalize.ts:184-198` only zeroes `block.id` and deletes marginTop/marginBottom), so if `markerToXml` stopped emitting `<a:buClr>` the re-imported marker would lose `color` and the deep-equality assertion would fail — i.e. the exact regression the reviewer says would pass CI is caught. The reviewer searched only `test/export/pptx/text.test.ts` and grepped for literal `buClr`/`marker:` in test files, missing the round-trip suite where the coverage is expressed through the XML fixture. Remaining uncovered slice is only the unnormalizable-color drop path for markers, whose underlying helper behavior is already asserted for runs (`test/export/pptx/text.test.ts:87+`, issue #728) — a minor breadth gap, not a blocking absence of coverage.
